claims.claim: **Chronic abdominal pain = intermittent or constant pain present for at least two months.** Usually, no organic cause turns up.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organic and functional causes are not mutually exclusive** — they can coexist and interact.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Comorbid anxiety and depression are very common**, and may both result from and contribute to chronic pain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask about associated symptoms:** unintentional weight loss or stunting · unexplained fever · change in bowel habit, chronic diarrhoea or blood in stools · nocturnal stooling · appetite change · dysphagia or odynophagia · persistent (especially bilious) vomiting · urinary symptoms · extraintestinal features of IBD.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also ask** about reflux symptoms, diet (including excluded foods), menstrual and sexual history where relevant, any IBD or coeliac disease in the family, a HEADSSS screen and the **functional impact on school and activities**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine:** hydration, pubertal status, weight and height (ideally serial), abdomen for palpable faeces or mass, and extraintestinal signs of IBD.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Organic causes are more likely if there are red flags.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Coeliac disease:** bloating, a change in bowel habit, slow growth or poor weight gain, iron deficiency resistant to treatment, family history.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Irritable bowel syndrome:** pain at least 4 days per month with a change in bowel habit, or related to defecation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Abdominal migraine:** stereotyped paroxysmal periumbilical or diffuse pain with few or no GI symptoms between attacks; migraine in the child or family.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Functional dyspepsia:** postprandial fullness, early satiety, epigastric pain or burning unrelated to bowel habit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Many children need no investigations**; target any testing to the likely diagnosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Faecal calprotectin for children over 4 years with IBD features.** Do not test under 4 years without discussing with a paediatrician or paediatric gastroenterologist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods, if indicated:** UEC, LFTs, CMP, lipase, TSH, glucose, coeliac serology with total IgA, ESR/CRP, FBE and ferritin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine imaging isn't needed**; the yield of abdominal ultrasound is very low, though it may exclude a mass when examination is abnormal or there are significant constitutional symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not perform abdominal X-rays for non-specific abdominal pain** — they are rarely helpful even for constipation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test for *H. pylori* only with peptic-ulcer red flags**, by stool antigen or urease breath test. **Do not use *H. pylori* serology.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflux symptoms in older children and adolescents: a 4-week PPI trial before referral may help.** Refer if not responding or unable to wean.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected IBD: get specialist advice and a paediatric gastroenterology referral.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Functional pain:** educate and reassure (no physical damage; most resolve with time and support); further tests and medicines are usually not needed; address psychosocial stressors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen for comorbid anxiety or depression** and consider mental health referral; **encourage return to function** (school, social, physical activity) and provide follow-up.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IBS, abdominal migraine, functional dyspepsia: refer to a specialist** for CBT/psychology, specialist dietitian input, gut-directed hypnotherapy, or medicines such as SSRI/low-dose TCA and antispasmodics. **No diet changes without professional advice.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Significant functional impairment** (poor school attendance, sleep disturbance, depression or anxiety): think about referring to adolescent medicine, a paediatrician or a paediatric chronic pain service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** if the child needs admission, has red flags or abnormal investigations.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** once red flags have been thought through, nothing concerning is found **and** clear follow-up is in place.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Abdominal pain - chronic' (Last updated March 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Abdominal_pain_-_chronic/, retrieved 2026-09-23
